details: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced their longest outflow streak on record, with investors pulling approximately $2.8 billion over nine consecutive days in late May. This indicates cooling institutional demand for Bitcoin. Despite these outflows, Bloomberg analysts note that Bitcoin's volatility is increasingly converging with gold, and BlackRock's IBIT ETF has largely outperformed US stocks since its approval.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Record Outflows; Volatility Nears Gold

details: Ethereum's price has been trading below $2,000 recently, indicating some short-term struggles. However, Standard Chartered maintains a bullish long-term outlook for ETH, projecting it to reach $4,000 by 2026 and $40,000 by 2030, citing strong underlying network activity.
title: Ethereum Under $2K, But Analysts Project $4K for 2026

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has filed a lawsuit against Nathan Fuller, the founder of Privvy Investments, for allegedly orchestrating a $12.3 million cryptocurrency fraud scheme. Fuller is accused of misleading around 150 investors with promises of high returns from non-existent AI trading bots and misappropriating funds for personal use.
title: SEC Charges Privvy Founder in $12.3M Crypto AI 'Bot' Scam

details: The Sui blockchain has experienced multiple mainnet halts recently, attributed to bugs encountered during network upgrades, some of which carried known risks of causing such disruptions. This instability has adversely affected the native SUI token, which has seen a 20% weekly decline and is now down over 83% from its all-time high.
title: Sui Network Mainnet Halts Due to Upgrade Bugs; SUI Token Drops 20%

details: The U.S. Treasury Secretary has announced the seizure of approximately $1 billion in Iranian cryptocurrency assets, stating that authorities "just outright grabbed the wallets." This action is part of "Operation Economic Fury," a broader campaign aimed at restricting Tehran's access to capital and enforcing international sanctions.
title: US Seizes $1 Billion in Iranian Crypto in Sanctions Push

details: According to a report by blockchain security firm CertiK, losses from cryptocurrency platform attacks plummeted by nearly 90% in May, totaling $68.3 million. This represents a significant decrease from April's $650 million in losses and marks the third month in 2026 where losses from hacks have remained under $100 million, indicating an improvement in overall security.
title: Crypto Hack Losses Drop 90% in May to $68.3 Million: CertiK
